Theme

House layout, roofs, rooms & furnishings

living room noun

also sitting room

classical

Vitruvius 5.11.2: exhedrae spatiōsae, habentēs sēdēs (so spelt in the Latin Library text)
Cicero, de Or. 3.17; N.D. 1.15 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 125

exedra, exedrae f.

noun, first declension

Classically a room furnished with seats, for conversation; in Cicero the room where the speakers of a dialogue sit and talk. Traupman gives it for “sitting room”. The e is short (Greek ἐξέδρα). Use it for the room’s function; summum tabulātum describes its position in the house.

Other words

  • mediānum, mediānī n. — the middle room

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · Dig. 9.3.5.2: ex mediānō cēnāculī (Lewis & Short, s.v. mediānus); Andresian p. 1

    In the Digest the middle part of an upper flat, not a named room; Andresian’s word for the living room. exedra is classical.

  • synoecium, synoeciī n. — a room shared by several people

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Petr. 93 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 124

    In Petronius a lodging where several people live together; Traupman uses it for a living room.

  • 1Traupman (pp. 124–125) gives sessōrium for “living room”, but its ancient senses are “seat, stool” (Caelius Aurelianus) and, in a single passage, “dwelling” (Petronius 77.4 vīperae hujus sessōrium) (Lewis & Short). Ruling: exedra for the sitting room.

    sessōrium1

    noun, second declension · avoid · modern · Traupman 124–125

Examples

  • Culīnam habet, cubicula, inter quae hospitium est, balneum, lātrīnam, hortum, trīclīnium, exedram

    It has a kitchen, bedrooms (among them a guest room), a bathroom, a lavatory, a garden, a dining room and a sitting roomcomposed

  • Hīc sedēbimus et colloquēmur.

    We’ll sit and talk here.composed
